tables.title: FORGE3DBench-150, 4 views
tables.dataset: FORGE3DBench-150 (150 objects from the 808-object benchmark, one per asset)
tables.protocol: obs-grounded reconstruction; baselines registered to ground truth; one run per method
notes: Every method reconstructs each object from the same input views (RGB and object masks) and the same cameras. Metrics: LPIPS/PSNR/SSIM on input-view (IV) renders and on a novel-view (NV) orbit, Chamfer-L1 in unit-cube units, F-score at threshold 0.01; each cell is the mean over objects that have every part.

Alignment: the shown baselines (ReconViaGen, Amodal3R, Hunyuan3D-2mv, Cupid) produce meshes in their own object frame, so each is registered to the ground-truth frame by a dense rotation search followed by rigid ICP, with an input-view silhouette tie-break; the pending Pixal3D row would be placed by camera only, since its output is pixel-aligned. FORGE3D is generated directly in the ground-truth frame and is not re-aligned.

Inputs differ in one respect: FORGE3D additionally uses the metric depth of the input views (oracle depth from the renderer, not predicted depth), while the baselines take RGB and masks only. FORGE3D is therefore grounded in the ground-truth frame through that depth; this is part of the method, not a like-for-like RGB-only comparison.

Input-view (IV) caveat: the IV reference is the shaded input image, while predictions are rendered unlit, which adds a roughly constant penalty for every method; absolute IV values are not meaningful and IV rewards methods that copy lighting baked into the input. Novel-view (NV) gaps are smaller than IV gaps.

Checkpoint and overlap: the FORGE3D rows come from one training run at a fixed checkpoint and a single sampling seed, and the numbers may change in the final paper. Whether the training data overlaps these evaluation objects has not been audited.
4 views = one frontal view plus three companion views, identical for every method.
Evaluated on n = 144 of the 150 selected objects: 6 objects have an untextured ground truth (no novel-view appearance reference), so they are excluded for every method.
Pixal3D row pending: its FORGE3DBench regeneration is not finished, so no number is shown.
Cupid: the released code is single-view; the multi-view variant here is our own implementation of the paper's multi-view fusion.
